review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

3:1.sourceText: Ἐν ἔτει δὲ πεντεκαιδεκάτῳ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Τιβερίου Καίσαρος, ἡγεμονεύοντος Ποντίου Πειλάτου τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Γαλιλαίας Ἡρῴδου, Φιλίππου δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Ἰτουραίας καὶ Τραχωνίτιδος χώρας, καὶ Λυσανίου τῆς Ἀβιληνῆς τετρααρχοῦντος,
3:1.targetText: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἡγεμονεύοντος ("governing") is rendered while … was governor.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The participle τετρααρχοῦντος ("ruling as tetrarch") is rendered tetrarch.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.
English lists the rulers with commas, so this καί and δέ have no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves χώρας ("region") untranslated after the two place names.

3:2.sourceText: ἐπὶ ἀρχιερέως Ἄννα καὶ Καϊάφα, ἐγένετο ῥῆμα Θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν Ζαχαρίου υἱὸν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.
3:2.targetText: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.

groups.note: The genitive ἀρχιερέως ("high priest") after ἐπί is rendered the high priesthood.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:3.sourceText: καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν περίχωρον τοῦ Ἰορδάνου κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν,
3:3.targetText: He went into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

3:4.sourceText: ὡς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ λόγων Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν Κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ·
3:4.targetText: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet:  “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:5.sourceText: πᾶσα φάραγξ πληρωθήσεται καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ βουνὸς ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ἔσται τὰ σκολιὰ εἰς εὐθείας καὶ αἱ τραχεῖαι εἰς ὁδοὺς λείας·
3:5.targetText: Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill made low. The crooked ways shall be made straight, and the rough ways smooth.

groups.note: ἔσται εἰς ("shall become") is rendered shall be made.
BSB's Greek text has a different form of this word here, with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
This second εἰς repeats the "shall become" construction, which English leaves understood.

3:6.sourceText: καὶ ὄψεται πᾶσα σὰρξ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
3:6.targetText: And all humanity will see God’s salvation.’”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:7.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν οὖν τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ὄχλοις βαπτισθῆναι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;
3:7.targetText: Then John said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending.

3:8.sourceText: ποιήσατε οὖν καρποὺς ἀξίους τῆς μετανοίας· καὶ μὴ ἄρξησθε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ· λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ Θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.
3:8.targetText: Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance. And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:9.sourceText: ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
3:9.targetText: The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

groups.note: ἤδη … κεῖται ("already lies") is rendered lies ready.
The inferential οὖν ("so") is rendered and.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δὲ καί ("and even") untranslated.

3:10.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες Τί οὖν ποιήσωμεν;
3:10.targetText: The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the quotation marks.

3:11.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὁ ἔχων δύο χιτῶνας μεταδότω τῷ μὴ ἔχοντι, καὶ ὁ ἔχων βρώματα ὁμοίως ποιείτω.
3:11.targetText: John replied, “Whoever has two tunics should share with him who has none, and whoever has food should do the same.”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … ἔλεγεν ("answering, he said") is rendered replied.
μή ("not") with ἔχοντι ("having") is rendered has none.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending.

3:12.sourceText: ἦλθον δὲ καὶ τελῶναι βαπτισθῆναι καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσωμεν;
3:12.targetText: Even tax collectors came to be baptized. “Teacher,” they asked, “what should we do?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering καί.
BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") untranslated.

3:13.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μηδὲν πλέον παρὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον ὑμῖν πράσσετε.
3:13.targetText: “Collect no more than you are authorized,” he answered.

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he".
τὸ διατεταγμένον ("what has been ordered") is rendered are authorized.
πράσσετε ("exact") is rendered Collect.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them") untranslated.

3:14.sourceText: ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ στρατευόμενοι λέγοντες Τί ποιήσωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς; καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Μηδένα διασείσητε μηδὲ συκοφαντήσητε, καὶ ἀρκεῖσθε τοῖς ὀψωνίοις ὑμῶν.
3:14.targetText: Then some soldiers asked him, “And what should we do?”  “Do not take money by force or false accusation,” he said. “Be content with your wages.”

groups.note: The καί of καὶ ἡμεῖς ("we too") is rendered by the opening And.
Μηδένα ("no one") is rendered by the negative.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this καί ("also") untranslated.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the quotation marks.
BSB puts the reply first and does not render this καί.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:15.sourceText: Προσδοκῶντος δὲ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ διαλογιζομένων πάντων ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν περὶ τοῦ Ἰωάνου, μή ποτε αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ Χριστός,
3:15.targetText: The people were waiting expectantly and were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.

groups.note: The name in περὶ τοῦ Ἰωάνου ("about John") and the pronoun αὐτός ("he") are both rendered John; BSB's Greek text spells the name differently.
μή ποτε ("whether perhaps") introduces the indirect question.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB folds "about John" into the question, so περί has no English word.

3:16.sourceText: ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων πᾶσιν ὁ Ἰωάνης Ἐγὼ μὲν ὕδατι βαπτίζω ὑμᾶς· ἔρχεται δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·
3:16.targetText: John answered all of them: “I baptize you with water, but One more powerful than I will come, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The present ἔρχεται ("is coming") is rendered as a future.
The resumptive αὐτοῦ ("his") repeats the relative οὗ; English expresses both with whose.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the colon.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves μέν untranslated; the following δέ gives but.

3:17.sourceText: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ διακαθᾶραι τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συναγαγεῖν τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην αὐτοῦ, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.
3:17.targetText: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”

groups.note: The relative οὗ ("whose") begins a new English sentence as His.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek clause has none.

3:18.sourceText: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἕτερα παρακαλῶν εὐηγγελίζετο τὸν λαόν·
3:18.targetText: With these and many other exhortations, John proclaimed the good news to the people.

groups.note: καί ("also") adds these many other exhortations to the sayings just reported.
The participle παρακαλῶν ("exhorting") is rendered with … exhortations.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves μὲν οὖν ("so then") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English points back to John's sayings just reported.
English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending.

3:19.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης, ἐλεγχόμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ περὶ Ἡρῳδιάδος τῆς γυναικὸς τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν πονηρῶν ὁ Ἡρῴδης,
3:19.targetText: But when he rebuked Herod the tetrarch regarding his brother’s wife Herodias and all the evils he had done,

groups.note: The passive participle ἐλεγχόμενος ("being rebuked") is recast as active, with John as subject.
ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ("by him"), the agent of the passive, becomes the English subject.
One regarding covers both περί phrases.
The repeated name Herod is rendered he.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative ὧν ("which") is left unexpressed in all the evils he had done.

3:20.sourceText: προσέθηκεν καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ πᾶσιν, κατέκλεισεν τὸν Ἰωάνην ἐν φυλακῇ.
3:20.targetText: Herod added this to them all: He locked John up in prison.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending.

3:21.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ βαπτισθῆναι ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν καὶ Ἰησοῦ βαπτισθέντος καὶ προσευχομένου ἀνεῳχθῆναι τὸν οὐρανὸν,
3:21.targetText: When all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized too. And as He was praying, heaven was opened,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("now it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:22.sourceText: καὶ καταβῆναι τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον σωματικῷ εἴδει ὡς περιστερὰν ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ φωνὴν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ γενέσθαι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.
3:22.targetText: and the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:23.sourceText: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσὴφ, τοῦ Ἡλεὶ
3:23.targetText: Jesus Himself was about thirty years old when He began His ministry.  He was regarded as the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,

groups.note: The participle ἀρχόμενος ("beginning") is rendered when He began.
The participle ὢν ("being") is absorbed into the English sentence, which names its subject as He.
The imperfect passive ἐνομίζετο ("was supposed") is rendered was regarded.
In the genealogy the article τοῦ stands for "the son", and the genitive name gives "of".
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
